brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1683085 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 124.8s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 28% over 30s (87/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,340/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 1683085) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,340/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: The root blocker pid 1683085 has been idle in transaction for 124.8s (DB-3), exceeding the business-tolerated 60s of degraded checkout (BIZ-1). Checkout success is 55% with $4,293/min at risk (BIZ-1). The blocking workload adhoc_reporting has no registry entry (BIZ-2), making termination risk unquantified. Given the prolonged block and missing workload information, escalation to the owning team is required for an informed trade-off assessment rather than risking unknown disruption by terminating or continuing to wait beyond the tolerated degradation window.

audit.report: The checkout flow degraded because an unknown workload adhoc_reporting acquired a lock held idle in transaction (pid 1683085), blocking 12 sessions and reducing checkout success to 55% (33/60 succeeded in the last 15s), later dropping to 28% (87/120 succeeded over 30s) against an SLO of 95%. Revenue at risk was $4,293/min, and the business tolerates at most 60 seconds of degraded checkout; the blocker persisted for 124.8s, exceeding this window. The adhoc_reporting workload had no entry in the workload registry, so owner, cost of interruption, and change-calendar status were unknown, preventing safe termination. After two rounds of evaluation, the Database Guardian initially recommended waiting, then escalated upon seeing the blocker exceed 60s, and the Continuity Guardian escalated to the on-call team; the ESCALATE action remains unexecuted, pending the owning team's decision.
audit.root_cause: The root cause was an unregistered adhoc_reporting workload that held an idle transaction (pid 1683085) for 124.8s, blocking 12 checkout sessions and exceeding the business's 60s tolerance for degraded performance.
lessons: Register all long-running batch and ad-hoc workloads (e.g., adhoc_reporting) in the workload registry at creation so owner, cost of interruption, and change-calendar status are known before a blocker exceeds tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian initially recommended waiting while the blocker was under 60s, but switched to escalate once the transaction persisted for 124.8s, correctly aligning with the business tolerance limit. The Continuity Guardian's invariant check correctly flagged the unknown interrupt cost of the unregistered adhoc_reporting workload, leading to escalation rather than a unilateral decision.
follow_ups: Add an entry for adhoc_reporting in the workload registry, capturing owner, estimated runtime, and interrupt cost, before the next incident.
Set a 30s alert threshold on the lock graph for transactions with active waiters, integrated with the RecoveryPact orchestrator.
Review and document the change-calendar coverage for adhoc_reporting, or establish a policy to prevent unregistered long-running transactions from blocking critical checkout paths.

Checkout success is 55% with $4,293/min at risk (BIZ-1). The blocking workload adhoc_reporting has no registry entry (BIZ-2), making termination risk unquantified. Given the prolonged block and missing workload information, escalation to the owning team is required for an informed trade-off assessment rather than risking unknown disruption by terminating or continuing to wait beyond the tolerated degradation window.

audit.report: The checkout flow degraded because an unknown workload adhoc_reporting acquired a lock held idle in transaction (pid 1683085), blocking 12 sessions and reducing checkout success to 55% (33/60 succeeded in the last 15s), later dropping to 28% (87/120 succeeded over 30s) against an SLO of 95%. Revenue at risk was $4,293/min, and the business tolerates at most 60 seconds of degraded checkout; the blocker persisted for 124.8s, exceeding this window. The adhoc_reporting workload had no entry in the workload registry, so owner, cost of interruption, and change-calendar status were unknown, preventing safe termination. After two rounds of evaluation, the Database Guardian initially recommended waiting, then escalated upon seeing the blocker exceed 60s, and the Continuity Guardian escalated to the on-call team; the ESCALATE action remains unexecuted, pending the owning team's decision.
audit.root_cause: The root cause was an unregistered adhoc_reporting workload that held an idle transaction (pid 1683085) for 124.8s, blocking 12 checkout sessions and exceeding the business's 60s tolerance for degraded performance.
lessons: Register all long-running batch and ad-hoc workloads (e.g., adhoc_reporting) in the workload registry at creation so owner, cost of interruption, and change-calendar status are known before a blocker exceeds tolerance.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian initially recommended waiting while the blocker was under 60s, but switched to escalate once the transaction persisted for 124.8s, correctly aligning with the business tolerance limit. The Continuity Guardian's invariant check correctly flagged the unknown interrupt cost of the unregistered adhoc_reporting workload, leading to escalation rather than a unilateral decision.
follow_ups: Add an entry for adhoc_reporting in the workload registry, capturing owner, estimated runtime, and interrupt cost, before the next incident.
